available_exact_identity_control.conflicting_label_policy: If one exact K79 signature has both binary labels within the currently authorized materialized universe, exclude all rows of that signature from scientific modeling/evaluation.
available_exact_identity_control.development_timing: Apply K79 conflict exclusion and duplicate collapse to the development universe BEFORE either RANDOM or CHRONOLOGICAL split.
available_exact_identity_control.duplicate_representative_policy: For same-label exact K79 duplicates, retain one deterministic representative: earliest source day, then smallest original zero-based row index within that source file.
available_exact_identity_control.fields: corrected timestamp second + all 78 Stage19 common numeric predictors
available_exact_identity_control.holdout_timing: The final holdout remains completely unopened during development. At the single authorized final opening, apply the already-frozen K79 rule to holdout rows. Exclude any holdout K79 signature already retained in development; then collapse same-label within-holdout duplicates deterministically. No development artifact may change.
available_exact_identity_control.implementation_hash_policy: Hash acceleration is permitted, but every candidate hash collision must be verified by exact canonical K79 field equality before rows are declared duplicates.
available_exact_identity_control.name: K79
available_exact_identity_control.numeric_canonicalization: Each of the 78 predictor tokens is stripped, parsed as IEEE-754 float64, and compared by exact parsed float64 value. NaN is one canonical missing token; +inf and -inf remain distinct canonical tokens. Any other numeric parse failure causes fail-closed abort.
available_exact_identity_control.purpose: Label-independent exact duplicate and cross-partition overlap control using only fields uniformly preserved by the historical Kaggle source.
available_exact_identity_control.timestamp_canonicalization: Apply the frozen Stage19.1C date correction rule, then encode the corrected timestamp at integer one-second resolution.
